item.title: Better access to new medicines must not mean worse access to care for most patients

item.title: Nuclear diplomacy continues to be structurally flawed because it excludes physicians
item.description: Agreement: I AgreeBody: Dear Editor The new round of nuclear diplomacy between the U.S. and Iran likely followed a very familiar script that we have come to know (1). Diplomats discussed enrichment levels, deterrence, regional security, and escalation risk. These talks had experts weighing in from all sides: intelligence, military, and foreign policy backgrounds. item.title: When standards shift mid-trial, primary care inherits the communication fallout
item.description: Agreement: I AgreeBody: Dear Editor, The report (1) on the FDA’s refusal to file Moderna’s application for the mRNA-1010 influenza vaccine highlights a familiar but under-discussed fault line in vaccine trials: when “standard of care” shifts, comparators become both a scientific and an ethical problem rather than a technical detail. item.title: Re: Management of obsessive-compulsive disorder in adults
item.description: Agreement: I AgreeBody: Dear Editor, This article goes straight from a description of symptoms of OCD to considering various treatments. OCD is described as a chronic or complex psychiatric condition, implying that it is due to a brain disorder. item.title: Widening the lens: genetic testing barriers risk compounding prostate cancer inequalities
item.description: Agreement: I AgreeBody: Dear Editor, I am very grateful to Naqvi and colleagues for highlighting the urgent need to address ethnic inequalities in prostate cancer outcomes.
